text:
micah: Quick ping — PR 6882 (microbatch scheduler tweak) is ready for review. I ran a canary yesterday and saw a small but consistent tail bump for short requests (<=64 tokens). p95 moved from ~22ms -> ~30-33ms in the canary. Need 2 approvals + agree on merge window. cc @ana-dev @lina @samir

ana-dev: Saw the CI results. Do you have the smoke/bench output? Can you paste the exact numbers and workload definition?

micah: Yep — pasted the smoke run below (same CPU/GPU types as prod canary pool). Workload: 1k short requests (10-40 tokens), concurrency=50, warmup 200. The only change is scheduler: prefer_microbatch_for_short=false -> true.

```
# smoke-bench: short-seq (concurrency=50)
requests: 1000
warmup: 200
model: rdlw-7b-int8
old: p50=11.2ms p95=22.4ms p99=45.8ms
new: p50=12.0ms p95=31.8ms p99=68.3ms
throughput: old=980 qps, new=940 qps
notes: tail widened; p50 stable-ish, p95 +9.4ms
```

lina: Hmm that's not huge but it's above our SLO for short paths (p95 < 30ms). Can we scope if this only impacts single-token prompts or all short prompts?

micah: I sliced by length — looks worse for 1-8 tokens: p95 ~38ms. For 20-40 tokens p95 ~28ms. So smallest requests pay the penalty. Likely microbatch wait jitter for tiny KV cache hits.

samir: Is this reproducible on local perf harness? If it's scheduling jitter we should be able to simulate with synthetic traffic. Also, any mem/dGPU utilization change?

micah: Repro'd on perf-harness with same qps. GPU util + mem unchanged. I added logging to scheduler: saw microbatch aggregation window spike from ~3-5ms -> 8-12ms under bursty load.

beth: Can we ship a config toggle to disable prefer_microbatch_for_short for now and roll it out? That'd be a quick mitigation while we root-cause. Also add a note to the release checklist.

micah: Yeah I can add a gate flag and a config knob. PR already has the flag but default flips to true; I'll add a runtime config override and test. Would prefer to merge the rest of the fix (other perf wins) and keep the flag off in canary.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary window: 1950040000 - 1950043600 UTC. Auto-rollback threshold: p95 short_seq > 30ms or error-rate +0.5%.

ana-dev: I'm fine approving once you push the runtime flag and a quick harness test showing canary with flag=false keeps p95 < 30ms. Also add a small note in the PR about follow-up investigation tasks.

samir: I can review the scheduler microbatch change. If you add the config I'll do a quick perf pass. One request: add a unit test for the microbatch timer compaction logic — it's a tiny harness.

micah: Will do. Plan: push small patch (flag default=false for canary), run perf harness, post results here. Aim to merge in the 2-hour merge window if all green.

beth: Approved pending tests + canary results. :thumbsup:

lina: Approving too given the mitigation plan. Please tag me if the canary shows regression so we can revert quickly.

micah: Uploaded new commit and harness run (flag=false):```
# quick-run with flag=false
new-flag=false
p50=11.4ms p95=23.1ms p99=46.2ms
throughput=975 qps
```

micah: Thanks all — requesting final approval from @samir and then I'll merge during 1950040500-1950041500 UTC window.

samir: Reviewing now, small nit but LGTM after adding the unit test.

micah: Added test, CI passed. Merging in the window. I'll monitor canary and post updates.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started. canary_id=c-2026-09-14-001.

micah: Canary steady so far (30m): p95 short_seq ~24ms, no error-rate increase. Will keep monitoring for next hour and then promote.

beth: Thanks for moving quickly. :tada:
